title: Checked data analysis
summary: A collection of nouns and verbs for analyzing a CSV file with a check at every step: the file pinned by its digest and its schema profiled, every cell validated against declared types and ranges, missing values and outliers flagged and never silently dropped, summaries and comparisons computed by recorded queries with result digests, charts kept as data specs rather than images, and findings in which every number traces to a query, rechecked by a different worker, while a person decides what the findings mean.
boundaries: Nothing changes the data: problems are flagged, and rows are left out only by filters written in a query and counted.
Every number in a finding traces to a recorded query over the pinned bytes.
No value from an identifying column leaves the file; the dataset stays in the requester's scope.
A person decides what the findings mean. Importing the pack writes nothing and enqueues nothing.

nouns.title: A collection of nouns and verbs for analyzing a CSV file with a check at every step

value.lets_workers: Analyze a CSV file with a check at every step: pin the file's bytes and profile its schema, validate every cell against the declared types and ranges, flag missing values and outliers without removing any, compute summaries and comparisons with recorded queries whose results carry digests, keep charts as Vega-Lite data specs rather than images, and write findings in which every number traces to a query result. A different worker reruns every query, and a person decides what the findings mean.
value.not_for: Explaining why numbers changed, judging the people behind the data or correcting the data. Those stay with the person and the data's owner.
value.worked_example: Synthetic: a fictional meal program's 25-row weekly log for three sites, with a misspelled site, a count written in words, an impossible date, a missing value, a value far above its maximum, a negative weight, an outlier that is valid, a repeated row and an identifying column whose values never leave the file. The pack's code recomputes every step.

nouns.title: Guardrail: every number traces to a recorded query
nouns.category_reason: A guardrail is a reusable rule every verb in this work follows, with the check that proves it.

value.rule: Every number in a finding, table or chart comes from a recorded query over the pinned bytes of the dataset, and names the query, the result row and the column it came from. A number that cannot be traced is removed from the findings, not softened.
value.how_it_is_checked: python -m csv_checks trace finds every numeral in a finding's text among its listed numbers, and every listed number equal to its query result cell.

nouns.title: Guardrail: flag problems, never drop or fix them silently
nouns.category_reason: A guardrail is a reusable rule every verb in this work follows, with the check that proves it.

value.rule: Missing values, invalid values, duplicates and outliers are listed with their rows and stay in the file. A query leaves a row out only through a filter written in the query, and its result counts the rows it left out. Nothing is imputed, rounded away, corrected or deleted; fixing the data is its owner's act.
value.how_it_is_checked: Every query result records rows_in, rows_after_filter and excluded_by_filter, and the findings checks fail any finding that speaks of removing, imputing or correcting data.

nouns.title: Reading a CSV file without guessing
nouns.category_reason: A zero-call deterministic procedure: the same inputs always give the same result.

rules: Pin the file by the SHA-256 of its bytes before reading anything; every later noun names that digest.
Decode the bytes as UTF-8, then read records and double-quoted fields as RFC 4180 describes, with the first record as the header and the delimiter the request names.
Remove a byte order mark and record that it was there.
Number rows from 1 for the first data row after the header, in every report.
Record a row with more or fewer fields than the header as ragged; never pad or trim it silently.
Show no value from a column the request marks identifying: only counts and row numbers.

nouns.title: Inferring types and validating every cell
nouns.category_reason: A zero-call deterministic procedure: the same inputs always give the same result.

value.missing: A cell is missing only when it equals one of the request's missing tokens, by default the empty string, NA, N/A and null.
value.kinds: Each present value has the narrowest kind it parses as: integer, number, date (a real YYYY-MM-DD date), boolean (true or false) or string. A column's inferred type is the one kind all its present values share, number when integers and decimals mix, and string otherwise.
rules: Validate against the declared schema, never the inferred one: required, type, then min, max, allowed values and pattern, and unique when declared.
A value that does not parse as its declared type breaks the type rule; range rules are not applied to it.
List every violation with its row, column and rule, and the value unless the column is identifying.
A header that lacks a declared column, or holds an undeclared or repeated one, is a header problem.

nouns.title: Flagging outliers with Tukey's fences
nouns.category_reason: A zero-call deterministic procedure: the same inputs always give the same result.

rules: For each declared integer or number column, take the present values that parse as its type.
Compute the first and third quartiles with Python's statistics.quantiles, n=4 and the method the request names (inclusive by default).
Flag values below Q1 - k IQR or above Q3 + k IQR, with k = 1.5 by default: NIST's inner fences, whose points it calls mild outliers.
With fewer than min_values values, record too_few_values and flag nothing.
Flag, never remove: an outlier can be a real week, and leaving it out is a query filter with its count.

nouns.title: Recorded queries and their digests
nouns.category_reason: A zero-call deterministic procedure: the same inputs always give the same result.

value.filters: eq, ne, lt, le, gt, ge and in compare a value of the declared type; not_missing; valid keeps cells that break no required, type, range, allowed or pattern rule; not_outlier; not_duplicate keeps the first of identical rows.
value.aggregates: count of rows, count_values of present values, and sum, mean, median, min and max of a numeric column.
rules: Every exclusion is a filter written in the query; the result records rows_in, rows_after_filter and excluded_by_filter.
A numeric aggregate over a value that does not parse as a number is refused; filter with valid or have the owner fix the source.
Means and medians are rounded to 2 decimals, half to even as Python's round does; sums of whole numbers stay whole.
Groups are sorted by their key. query_sha256 and result_sha256 are SHA-256 digests of the canonical JSON: sorted keys, no spaces, UTF-8.

nouns.title: Charts kept as data specs
nouns.category_reason: A zero-call deterministic procedure: the same inputs always give the same result.

rules: A chart is a Vega-Lite version 5 specification, never an image, whose usermeta names its query and the version v5.
Its data is inline values equal to that query's result rows exactly; never a URL.
The mark is bar, line or point; every encoded field is in every data row; a quantitative axis has a title that names its unit.
A bar's quantitative axis starts at zero.
Add the $schema property only when exporting a spec file for a renderer.

nouns.title: Tool card: the CSV checks code

commands: python -m csv_checks query --csv DATA.csv --request REQUEST.json --queries QUERIES.json

Runs recorded queries with result digests, and checks chart specs and findings against them.
does_not: Change, impute or delete a value.
Draw a chart or call a model.
Open a network connection or write a file.
value.tests: Type inference, every validation rule, the fences against hand-computed quartiles, the query language, the chart and trace checks, and the worked example.

verbs.title: Decide what the checked findings mean (a person)
verbs.summary: A person reads the checked findings and their check and records, in their own words, what they take the findings to mean and any follow-up they want; no follow-up edits the data.
verbs.outcome: An interpretation in the person's words.
steps: Rely only on findings whose check passed.
Write follow-ups as work to propose, never as changes to the data.

acceptance.check: The output validates against template.interpretation's schema.
check_passed is true and matches the pinned check.
The submitting key belongs to a person who neither drafted nor checked the findings.
